input.brief: Roafix, civic app in Tijuana: citizens report a pothole with a photo and GPS, and the pending reports appear on a public map

direction.name: The sentence is the layout
direction.idea: One short sentence, set at poster scale, is the composition. The trick that makes it an idea rather than a big headline: something from the subject sits inside the sentence where a word would be. A strip of photograph fills the gap between two words; a small live fragment of the product replaces the noun; the object the sentence names is pictured at the size of a letter. Write the sentence first, find the word that can be shown instead of said, and put the showing in its place. The reader completes the sentence with their eyes.
direction.composition: The sentence is four to seven words and runs as one or two full-width lines at 9–13vw. Inline with the type, on the baseline, sits one media slot: a rounded-rectangle or square frame exactly one line-height tall and two to three ems wide, holding a photograph or a looping crop. Above and below the sentence the screen is empty except for a small navigation line and one supporting sentence set small, both on the same left margin. Later sections repeat the grammar at smaller scale: each is a short statement on the left six columns with its proof (image, figure, list) on the right, so the page reads as a series of sentences with evidence. Generous vertical space (160px or more) between sections.
direction.typography: Display weight with real presence (medium to bold), tracking -0.03 to -0.05em, leading 0.95–1.0 so two lines sit close. The inline frame aligns to cap height and baseline exactly; set it with em units so it scales with the type.
direction.colour: A calm ground with ink at full contrast. The only colour comes from the photograph inside the sentence; if the palette has an accent, use it once, on the action.
direction.imagery: One strong, simple photograph that reads at small size (a face, an object, a texture, a horizon), cropped to a wide strip inside the sentence. The same image may open to full width in the next section, so the small slot feels like a window onto something larger.
direction.richness: The collision of big type and one live image inside it. Because there is only one image on the first screen, choose it with care and give it perfect alignment to the letters.
direction.pitfalls: The sentence must be short enough for two lines on a phone, where the inline frame drops to its own line between the two halves. Do not style one word differently to fake the device. Do not use more than one slot per sentence.

hero.name: Photograph for a letter
hero.blueprint: A flat white or pale ground, about 85% empty. The name sits on one line at the exact vertical centre, bold, at clamp(96px, 10.5vw, 168px), tracking -0.04em, spanning 78–88% of the width with equal side margins. One photograph is set into the line as if it were a glyph. Either it fills the word space between first and last name (a landscape frame one x-height tall and about 1.6em wide, resting on the baseline), or it replaces one round letter of a short name (a square frame exactly one cap-height tall). Build the line as an inline-flex row with `align-items: baseline` and size the frame in em so it scales with the type; square corners, `object-fit: cover`. Navigation is small and pushed to the edges: a 15px wordmark or monogram top-left at a 24px margin and up to five text links at 14px spread evenly across the right half of the top edge. Along the bottom edge, on the same margin: one supporting sentence at 16px starting at column 6, and the single action as an underlined text link flush right.
hero.mobile: The name stacks on two centred lines at 19vw with line-height 0.9. The photograph leaves the line and becomes a 3:2 frame at full width minus 16px margins between the two lines, so the screen reads word, picture, word. A single short name keeps the square frame inline at cap height instead. The supporting sentence and action sit under the block at 16px; the links collapse to one word top-right.
hero.headline: The name on one line with a photograph in its word space or in place of one letter, up to about 16 characters at 10.5vw, splitting into two lines on a phone.

motion.name: Shutter image
motion.description: The one hero or showcase image opens from an edge with a clip-path over about 1.1 seconds while the picture inside settles from 1.12 scale to rest. Use it once, on the image that matters most; later images simply are there. Recipe: 'Image shutter' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: Portrait as drop cap
sections.blueprint: No heading. One biography paragraph of 50–80 words is set large at clamp(24px, 2.5vw, 38px), regular weight, leading 1.2, across columns 3–12 of the grid. A square portrait is floated at the paragraph's start with `float: left`: its side equals three lines of text (3.6em), with 0.5em of space to its right, so the first three lines wrap beside it and the fourth returns to the paragraph's left edge, like a drop capital. Square corners. The person's name, the first words of the paragraph, is in full ink; the rest may be in a softer ink with linked names in full ink and underlined. A second paragraph follows after one blank line in the soft ink at the same size. Columns 1–2 hold three short facts (place, since when, how to reach) at 14px, top-aligned with the portrait. Section padding 140px.
sections.mobile: Text at 22px with leading 1.25, full width. The portrait keeps its float but grows to four lines tall, about 110px square. The three facts move below the second paragraph as a single row of three small blocks at 13px.

sections.name: Headline you can type
sections.blueprint: The section's headline is an input. One line at clamp(48px, 8vw, 132px), tight tracking, flush left across columns 1–12, is a real `<input>` (root marked data-ui) with no border and no fill, prefilled with a believable two-to-five-word example of what a user gives the product: a search, a question, a date in words, a colour name. A solid caret block 0.08em wide blinks after the last character. 48px beneath, on the same left edge, the product's answer appears at true interface size, at most 560px wide: three result rows, one parsed value, or a swatch, updating as the visitor types. Bottom-left, three more examples at 17px act as plain text buttons that refill the line. The rest of the 88svh field is empty. If the text outgrows the line it scrolls inside the input; it never wraps.
sections.mobile: The input is set at 11vw on one line and scrolls sideways inside itself when the text runs long. The answer follows 28px below at full width and true size. The three examples become a wrapping row of filled blocks 44px tall beneath the answer; tapping one refills the line.

sections.name: Drag through the stages
sections.blueprint: A 50/50 split, 88svh tall: two flat fields meeting on a clean vertical edge, and one slider that drives both. Left field: the current stage as a clause of three to six words at clamp(40px, 4.6vw, 76px) on two lines, top-left from column 1, starting with its order word; it serves as the heading. Right field: one fragment of the product at true size, about 440px wide, centred, root marked data-ui, in the state that matches the clause. Along the bottom, crossing both fields inside 28px margins, a real range `<input>` with four stops: a solid track 8px tall, the part already passed in full ink, and a square thumb 32px across in the accent. Under the track, four stage names at 16px, the current one in full ink. Dragging, or the arrow keys, swaps the clause and the fragment's state with a 200ms crossfade; nothing depends on scroll.
sections.mobile: The fragment's field comes first, 46svh, the fragment at true size and cropped to its active region. The slider follows directly beneath on the seam, thumb 40px. Then the clause field: the clause at 9vw on two lines, with the four stage names under it in a two-by-two block at 15px.

sections.name: Prints dropped on the headline
sections.blueprint: A flat colour field 100svh tall. A two-line headline of two to four words in an ultra-condensed or ultra-heavy face is centred, each line clamp(120px, 14vw, 210px) tall with leading 0.85. Two portrait photographs, each about 26vw wide at 3:4 with an 8px solid white border like a print, are absolutely placed on top of the headline's centre: one rotated −8 degrees, one +6 degrees, overlapping each other by a third and hiding roughly half the letters, so the eye completes the words. A third, smaller print (16vw) may sit at the lower right, cropped by the section's bottom edge. One plain sentence at 16px sits at the bottom-left margin, 24px from the edges. The prints are above the type in the stacking order; hovering one brings it to the front and straightens it to 0 degrees over 200ms. Nothing else is on the field.
sections.mobile: Headline lines at 30vw, still two lines, centred in a 78svh field. Two prints only, each 52vw wide, rotated −6 and +5 degrees, overlapping at the headline's centre. The small sentence sits at the bottom-left margin at 15px.

sections.name: Names as one sentence
sections.blueprint: Client, press or partner names are written out as one run-on sentence and set large: clamp(40px, 5vw, 76px), leading 1.0, flush left across all twelve columns, wrapping naturally over five to seven lines. Names are separated by commas and the list ends with a full stop. All names are set in a dimmed ink (still at least 3:1 against the ground), so the block reads as texture; one name at a time is lit in the full ink, and the lit name moves through the list every two seconds (a class toggled by a short script, with a 400ms colour transition). The sentence opens with two or three plain words in the full ink that act as the heading: the phrase that introduces the names. Nothing else is in the section: no logos, no columns, and 120px of space above and below.
sections.mobile: The same sentence at 9vw, wrapping over ten to fourteen lines; cut the list to the twelve strongest names so it stays within one and a half screens. The lit name still cycles. Margins are 20px and there are no other elements.

sections.name: Sentence, portrait, two links
sections.blueprint: One closing row of three elements hanging from the same top line, with open ground between them, on a 12-column grid. Columns 1–5: a sentence of 12–18 words at clamp(26px, 3vw, 44px), four lines, leading 1.1, saying what kind of enquiries are welcome; it is set as a paragraph and there is no separate heading. Columns 8–9: one small square portrait or photograph of the place, 150–170px, with square corners. Columns 10–12: a short question at 18px in medium weight, then 20px below it two underlined links stacked at 18px (the email address and one booking or social link), and beneath them a line at 14px in the soft ink with the city and the usual reply time. Columns 6–7 stay empty. The row has 160px of space above and 120px below. No form. On a dark ground the photograph is the only bright thing in the row.
sections.mobile: The sentence comes first at 7.4vw. Below it the portrait at 96px square sits at the left margin with the question and the two links to its right, top-aligned, in the remaining width. The city and reply-time line spans the full width beneath.

sections.name: Wide heading, indented questions
sections.blueprint: A heading of three to five words at about 5.5vw runs from the left margin on one or two lines and is the only large thing in the section. 80px beneath it the questions begin, indented to start at column 5 and running to column 12, so the left third under the heading stays empty. Each question is a row at 22–24px in the regular weight with a chevron of two 2px strokes at the far right; rows are separated by 36px of space and no rules. Opening a row lays a tile of the one-step tone behind that row and its answer (24px padding, extending 24px beyond the text on both sides) and shows the answer at 17px with a 48ch measure. Six questions. Nothing else shares the screen; the indent against the wide heading is the composition. Build with `<details>`.
sections.mobile: The heading sits at 10vw on two lines. Questions lose the indent and run full width at 19px with 28px between rows; the open row keeps its tone tile, now bleeding to both screen edges, with the answer at 16px inside it.

sections.name: The idea again, inverted
sections.blueprint: The close flips the page's colours: ink becomes the ground and the ground becomes the ink, across a full-bleed field at least 90svh tall. The page's opening idea returns as a headline of three to five words at 9–11vw on two lines, leading 0.9, flush left, positioned in the upper two-thirds; it should echo the hero's wording, not repeat it. Along the bottom, on one shared baseline 40px above the edge: one supporting sentence at 20px in columns 1–5 and one rectangular button in the accent colour, right-aligned in columns 10–12, about 56px tall. Nothing else: no image, no second button, no logo. The field's top edge is a hard horizontal line where it meets the section above. If the footer follows on the same inverted field, leave 160px before it so the close still reads as its own screen.
sections.mobile: The same inverted field at 80svh. Headline at 15vw on two lines at the top. The sentence sits lower at 17px, and the button spans the full width at the bottom, 56px tall, with 20px margins. Nothing else is added.

sections.name: Invitation over a cropped name
sections.blueprint: Close and footer in one full-viewport field of the inverse colour. Upper third, columns 1–7: a two-line invitation at about 5vw, three to five words, with one filled rectangular button beneath it. At columns 10–12, top-aligned with the invitation, three or four social or contact links stacked at 16px. The wordmark fills the bottom of the screen at 26–30vw on one line, `white-space: nowrap`, heavier and larger than the viewport can hold: it is pushed down with `transform: translateY(30%)` so the bottom edge cuts through the letters, and a long name also runs off the right edge. `overflow: hidden` on the footer does the cropping. One row of credits and legal links at 13px sits directly above the wordmark's cap line, spread left and right. The cropped name must be recognisable from its upper two-thirds alone; test that it is.
sections.mobile: Invitation at 11vw on two lines at the top with a full-width button. Links follow as one row of words at 15px. The wordmark sits at 34vw at the bottom, cropped by both the bottom and the right edge, with the legal row above it at 12px.

references.name: Colonia Zacamil
references.idea: The sentence is the layout: 'FLY TO ___ ZACAMIL' runs as one full-width line, with a strip of drone video filling the gap where a word would sit.
references.hero: Warm off-white field with no navigation at all. One line of black ultra-condensed capitals about 13vw tall sits on the vertical centre and runs edge to edge with 28px side margins: 'FLY', a wide gap, 'TO', then a rounded-corner strip of aerial video exactly as tall as the letters and half the viewport wide, then 'ZACAMIL'. A tiny mono bracket label sits above the last word. About 150px lower, a small black pill button with a white dot-in-circle at its right end is centred. Two centred lines of 24px serif sit near the bottom edge. The top third is empty.
references.type: Heathergreen, an ultra-condensed regular-weight sans, in capitals at 187px; Reckless Neue serif at 24px for the caption; Roboto Mono for the button and bracket label. Three faces, each used once, with roughly an 8:1 jump and no tracking adjustments.
references.colour: #ebe6e0 #000000 #3d4633 #8d8a84 #4d8fa3 — Warm putty paper with pure black type and button. The only colour on the page is inside the video strip: tree greens, roof greys and one patch of teal.
references.imagery: Top-down drone footage of housing blocks and trees, cropped to an extreme letterbox near 5:1 with 14px rounded corners and used as a word inside the headline; on mobile it becomes a 2:1 block between two headline lines.
references.layout: Single viewport, no scroll captured. Everything hangs on the central axis: full-width headline line mid-screen, button below, caption at the foot. About 80% of the screen is bare paper. On mobile the sentence stacks into three bands: words, video, word.
steal: Replace a word in the headline with a media strip cut to the cap height, so the picture is read as part of the sentence.
Use three type voices once each (ultra-condensed display, soft serif caption, mono button) instead of one family in many sizes.
On mobile, restack the same sentence as word / image / word at full width rather than shrinking the single line.

references.name: bleibtgleich’26
references.idea: One thin vertical rule runs down the page and a tight bold grotesk sentence wraps around it, words stepping from one side of the line to the other.
references.hero: White page, black type. Content sits in a narrow band between 26% and 68% of the width. A 1px vertical rule drops from the top edge at 37% for two-thirds of the height. Left of it: a black blob avatar at the top, a tiny role caption at its foot. Right of it: a tiny location note at the top, the name in two lines of 90px medium grotesk at the bottom. The tagline continues below at the same size, flush to the band's left edge, running past the fold. The upper half is otherwise blank. The handle is split into two pale-grey words fixed in the bottom corners; a black menu pill sits top-right.
references.type: Akzidenz Grotesk Pro medium only, -0.05em tracking, line-height about 0.9. Two sizes: 90px (6.3vw) for every statement and 11-13px for captions and table rows, a 7:1 jump. Long words are hyphenated and stepped across lines on purpose.
references.colour: #ffffff #000000 #e4e4e4 #f2f2f2 — Black on white with no accent. Pale grey is used for the ghosted corner wordmark and a few small square tiles; tiny coloured rings inside those tiles are the only hue.
references.imagery: Almost none: a black blob avatar, a few 85px grey tiles each with a coloured ring, and a canvas dome of small tilted project thumbnails floating between two words.
references.layout: Everything hangs off one vertical axis at 37%: lines start either at the axis or one indent to its left, giving a stepped rag. Very wide white margins. Sections are separated by a full screen of white rather than rules or colour.

sections.description: A 90px sentence is typeset word by word around the vertical rule: one word ends just left of the rule, the next starts just right of it, and the following line is centred beneath both. Above the sentence a row of five 85px pale-grey squares, each with a small coloured ring at its centre, is spaced unevenly along one baseline, with a three-line 13px description under the second.

The heading first appears as one centred line near the bottom of an empty screen, then its two halves separate to the far left and far right edges at mid-height. In the gap a WebGL dome of fifteen or so small project thumbnails, mostly black and white, tilts in perspective like tiles on a sphere. Nothing else is on the screen.

The heading is broken into an ampersand alone in the left margin and two words stepped over three lines with a hyphen break and a growing indent. Below it a four-column table at 11px: year, site name, awarding body, award. Hairline rules sit under every row, columns align to the hero's band, and year groups are separated by a blank row.

The closing sentence is stepped over four lines with shifting indents, right of centre. To its left two tiny grey captions and an email address at 11px. Under it three 36px outlined circles with social initials, centred, then the handle at about 44px centred on the bottom edge with tiny legal text in the two corners.

steal: Draw one 1px vertical rule and typeset a large sentence around it, alternating words to either side so the line becomes the text's spine.
Split the logotype into two words, ghost them at about 10% grey, and fix one in each bottom corner of the viewport.
Leave the top half of the hero blank and start the name at 50% height so the headline runs off the fold and pulls the scroll.
references.media: No picture on the first screen, which is all type plus a small black mark. Pictures arrive later as a WebGL sphere of project thumbnails flanked by two words that slide apart on scroll, square tiles placed on separate grid cells with empty cells between them, hover thumbnails behind a text index, and one small image used as a glyph in a row of numerals; no video.
references.motion: A 2.5s progress counter runs although the page loaded in 1.5s, while a vertical line draws down with the role label at its tip. Lenis and 15 ScrollTriggers with nothing pinned: display lines rise by yPercent over 0.47s in-out at a 0.075s stagger, the globe's rotation is scrubbed across its 1178px block, the flanking words are pulled apart on a scrub, and underlines wipe in by background-size over 0.6s cubic-bezier(0.76,0,0.24,1).

references.name: ARCHIV
references.idea: A waitlist page as a museum plinth: one cut-out everyday object at a time, centred on off-white beneath a heavy serif wordmark.
references.hero: Off-white single screen with no scroll. A heavy high-contrast serif wordmark in black caps sits top-left at a 56px margin, about 410px wide (28% of the viewport) and 80px tall. Opposite, top-right at the same margin, one line of 14px sans description aligns with the wordmark's top. Dead centre, one photographed object (a painted wooden pepper mill about 140px wide and 440px tall) stands on a barely visible lighter rounded square with a soft contact shadow; other objects replace it in turn. Below, a centred 11px grey line, then a white rounded email field 236px wide with a circled arrow inside its right end. Roughly 80% is empty.
references.type: The wordmark is drawn lettering in a heavy display serif with tight spacing, cap height about 5.5vw. All live text is Helvetica Neue regular at 14px and about 11px, black or grey. Two text sizes only; the contrast is wordmark against near-invisible interface text.
references.colour: #f1efec #000000 #ffffff #d9261c #e8a317 #7a7a75 — Warm off-white field, black wordmark, a white input; all colour arrives through whichever object is showing (red and yellow mill, tan leather, blue cap).
references.imagery: Studio cut-outs of single everyday objects in three-quarter view with a soft grounded shadow on matching off-white, each scaled to similar visual mass and centred, one at a time, no frame.
references.layout: One fixed viewport with four elements: wordmark top-left, description top-right, object in the exact centre, form bottom-centre. Margins of 56px, no rules, nav or footer. On mobile the wordmark centres and the description disappears.

sections.description: The central object rotates through unrelated things (pepper mill, sling chair, sticker-covered hydrant, layered iced drink, record player, baseball cap), each photographed in the same light and replaced in place within a zone roughly 250-300px square. Shadow direction and visual weight stay constant, so the object is the page's only variable and no carousel controls are needed.

Beneath the object, a centred line of 11px grey text, a 30px gap, then a white field about 236 by 52px with 12px radius: light grey placeholder at left and a 26px circle-outlined arrow as the submit control inside the right end. No button label, border or shadow; the field is the only pure white on the page, which marks it as the one interactive thing.

steal: Build a pre-launch page from four elements only (wordmark top-left, one-line description top-right, a single centred object, an email field) and leave the rest of the screen empty.
Cycle one consistently lit cut-out object in the same spot to show range without adding a grid or carousel controls.
Make the email field the only pure-white element on an off-white page, with submit as a circled arrow inside it rather than a labelled button.
